summary: Reproduced the sync and async trace-context loss across an uninitialized pickle relay. Fixed it by preserving the serialized wire state in relay-only processes so an initialized scheduler or detokenizer can reconstruct the live context. Rejected the open upstream PR's router-initialization approach after a real gfx950 serving run showed that initializing OpenTelemetry before process creation risks inherited set-once providers and missing exporter threads after fork.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=python /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-5f01ee817cc7/venv/bin/python - <<'PY' ... two-hop sync/async pickle reproduction ... PY
tests.what_was_measured: Before the change, both initialized destinations received tracing_enable=False after an uninitialized relay; raw output is /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-5f01ee817cc7/evidence/failing-before.txt. After the change, both received tracing_enable=True; raw output is /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-5f01ee817cc7/evidence/passing-after.txt.
58 focused unit tests passed, including sync and async two-hop relay regressions and an independently disabled-context boundary. Raw output: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-5f01ee817cc7/evidence/unit-final.txt.

The qualified deterministic tiny Llama executed HTTP generation and real GPU prefill/decode on gfx950. This probe tested and rejected the upstream router-initialization candidate: scheduler spans were not retained by the collector, consistent with OpenTelemetry provider/exporter state being inherited across fork. Logs: /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-5f01ee817cc7/evidence/sync-after/server.log and async-after/server.log.

gpu_execution.evidence: AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950 identification is in /tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-5f01ee817cc7/evidence/gpu.txt. Server logs record successful model load, Triton compilation, GPU prefill batches, decode, and HTTP 200 generation with the exact multi-worker topology.

remaining_limitations: The final serialization-preserving fix is verified against the exact failing pickle boundary and focused tests, but was not re-run through a successfully retained end-to-end OTLP collector capture after the earlier router-initialization candidate was rejected. The tiny random Llama validates transport and engine execution only; it does not validate semantic accuracy, another architecture, or a distributed workload.
